review_notes: I read the whole example file, the general PrimeDiscriminants.lean file, and the signatures of the odd and even prime-discriminant Legendre lemmas in Basic.lean. I found no repeated nontrivial reasoning. The only repetition is instantiating existing API (the even and odd prime-discriminant iff lemmas) inside the mp/mpr and fin_cases scaffolding. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that any rewrite compiles.

claims.reason: The repeated block is five instantiations (mp and mpr, so ten uses) of one existing lemma, `legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff`, plus one `simpa [oddPrimeDiscriminant]` normalisation. All the mathematical content, quadratic reciprocity for odd prime discriminants and the supplementary law for -4, already sits in Basic.lean and EvenPrimeDiscriminant.lean. The proposed helper `legendreSym q D = 1 ↔ legendreSym p q = 1` given `D = oddPrimeDiscriminant p` is `subst hD; exact legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff hp hq`. That is a thin wrapper around existing API, which the rubric says is insufficient. It also moves the work rather than removing it. Each of the entries 5, -3 and -7 would still need its own `hD : (c : ℤ) = oddPrimeDiscriminant p` proof (by simp or decide) and its own `hp` side goal (by norm_num). The `simpa [oddPrimeDiscriminant]` unfolding, which is the only per-entry step, would therefore be spelled out once per entry anyway. The second part of the proposal, replacing `constructor`/`fin_cases` with `Fin.forall_fin_succ` and `and_congr`, is a restructuring of case branches. That counts as moving duplicated branches, not as a shared lemma. The file is two small worked examples of 20 to 30 lines each, and the rest is routine instantiation. A general lemma already exists for the family form (`forall_legendreSym_primeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff`, and the odd-only `forall_legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff`). Its output is existential and `if`-shaped, so the concrete examples are meant to expose the clean congruence statements directly. A third example would be a short, mechanical copy, and the finding gives no evidence that a non-routine argument repeats.

legendreSym q (oddPrimeDiscriminant p) = 1 ↔ legendreSym p (q : ℤ) = 1 := by
  rw [legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_legendreSym hp hq]

simpa [oddPrimeDiscriminant] using
        (legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff
          (p := 5) (q := p) (by norm_num) hodd).mp h1

simpa [oddPrimeDiscriminant] using
          (legendreSym_oddPrimeDiscriminant_eq_one_iff
            (p := 3) (q := p) (by norm_num) hodd).mp h1
